story.title: Automatic payment retry on PSP failure
story.description: Context:  A temporary PSP outage (timeout, 5xx) fails the order outright today: customer sees an error, cart is abandoned, support tickets follow. The order service already distinguishes PSP decline from PSP error, so a legitimate retry is identifiable.    Reason:  Payment errors were 38% of abandoned carts last quarter; the payments team estimates roughly a fifth are transient PSP failures. Support receives ~120 payment-failure tickets/month; halving that saves about 2 agent-days per month.    Scope:  Automatic retry for PSP errors only. Out of scope: retries for declines, changes to the decline messaging, native apps.
acceptance_criteria: Given a payment that failed due to a PSP error (not a decline), when the failure is handled, then the system retries the payment automatically without customer action.
Given a retried payment that succeeds or a failure that is a decline, when the outcome is known, then retries stop immediately.
Given retries exhausted, when the last attempt fails, then the customer sees the standard payment-failed page and the order remains recoverable from the cart.
Given any retried payment, when it completes (success or final failure), then the retry outcome is visible in the existing payments dashboard.

findings.title: Retry Policy (Count and Delay) is Undefined
findings.description: The acceptance criteria mention retries can be exhausted but do not specify the number of retries, the delay between them, or the backoff strategy.

findings.title: User Experience During In-Flight Retries is Unspecified
findings.description: The story does not define what the customer sees while automatic retries are in progress; the total wait time may exceed thirty seconds with no feedback.

current.based_on_extra_context: Retry policy from the payments team: max 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 5s, 25s), every attempt carries the same PSP idempotency key per order, and the cart is held for 5 minutes from the first failure. Retries stop on success or decline as written.

findings.title: User Experience During In-Flight Retries is Unspecified
findings.description: The previous review raised the risk of a user manually re-submitting payment during an automatic retry. The provided context defines the backend retry policy (max 3 attempts, exponential backoff, ~31s total) and use of an idempotency key, but the user experience during these in-flight retries is still unspecified.

findings.title: Data Requirements for Payments Dashboard are Vague
findings.description: AC4 requires the retry outcome visible in the existing payments dashboard but does not specify what data constitutes the outcome.
